clue.text: Unconventional escape route

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means offbeat or eccentric
an exit, the route by which one leaves

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the same hyphenated phrase: slang for eccentric, and literally an exit.

clue.text: A drip at a time, one continuously stirring

parts.note: a drip is a feeble person, and git a contemptuous word for one
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means without stopping, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Water dripping one drop at a time keeps something constantly stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is the act of stirring or shaking a liquid, as a washing machine does.

clue.text: Visual flash mostly seen in shimmering stone

indicators.note: something seen in a thing is inside it, so one piece goes within the stone

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone with a shimmering play of colours

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: in a flash and in a tick both mean in an instant

explanation.surface: A flash of light glimpsed in a glittering gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight or vision, so it is a synonym of visual.

clue.text: Narrow passage up in tower?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel of water, a strait

explanation.surface: A tight stairway climbing a castle turret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' suggests a building, but read it as one who tows: the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a boat that tows ships, so it is literally something that tows.

clue.text: Metal instrument one held by belly

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

indicators.note: one piece is gripped inside another, the belly holding the one

parts.note: tum is a colloquial word for the belly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician's instrument is a metal one, cradled against a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutetium is a chemical element, a rare-earth metal named after Paris.

clue.text: Slackening of uphill express train in Chicago

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means reading the letters from the bottom up

parts.note: to express a thought is to put it into words
the El is Chicago's elevated railway

explanation.surface: An express train slowing down as it climbs a gradient in Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express train' looks like one phrase but splits: 'express' is PUT and 'train in Chicago' the El.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing off, so it is a slackening of effort or intensity.

clue.text: Fast pulse to help vigorous, hard ' creature when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: aid means help
racy means lively and vigorous
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a cat is a creature

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat helps a strong animal climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'creature' is a print blemish. 'when climbing' turns AID, RACY, H and CAT all upside down together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tachycardia is the medical term for an abnormally rapid heart rate.

clue.text: Mount exercises and cause ruin

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
PE is physical education, school exercises
to do harm is to cause it

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain as exercise causes ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck it, a figurative use of the naval weapon.

clue.text: Tasteful narrowing in the middle of a bone

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of these words, straddling them

explanation.surface: An elegant tapering in the middle of a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar describes the ulna, the forearm bone on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Leak-proof boat's ultimate in first class privilege

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class, as in Lloyd's Register ratings of ships

indicators.note: the final letter of the boat goes inside the word for privilege

parts.note: a right is an entitlement or privilege

indicators.note: ultimate picks the last letter of the word it governs

explanation.surface: A watertight boat being the last word in first-class luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airtight lets nothing escape, so it is sealed against leaks.

clue.text: Recaps only blunders, dropping off complaint

indicators.note: a blunder is a botched job, so these words come out jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who only rehashes earlier work keeps making mistakes, a complaint about a lazy reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' reads as part of the complaint about blunders, but it means falling asleep: the definition is a disorder that makes you nod off.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcolepsy is a medical condition in which the sufferer falls asleep suddenly and uncontrollably.

clue.text: Flexible about retaining half of clinic to make a crust.

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: lithe means supple, flexible

indicators.note: half of means only the first four of the eight letters stay

parts.note: a hospital is a clinic
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A supple dough built around a clinic's leftovers makes a pastry crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps HOSP from HOSPITAL; it sits inside LITHE, followed by RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The lithosphere is the rigid outer shell of the earth, its crust and upper mantle.

clue.text: Bring home in sound vessel

indicators.note: sound here means heard rather than seen, so the vessel's word is said out loud

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Fetching something home inside a solid, seaworthy vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (a sound vessel is a seaworthy ship), but it signals a homophone: URN and the answer sound alike in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring home a wage is to earn it, an everyday idiom for income.

clue.text: Six nips making you good and sick?

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Six drinks of spirits make you feel fine and then poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: A gill is an old British liquor measure, a quarter of a pint; spirits were once served in nips of a sixth of a gill, so six nips make one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill is the old measure equal to six of the small whisky measures called nips.

clue.text: Brownish-red peels from the tikka with shredded carrot in

indicators.note: the jumbled vegetable goes inside the letters taken from the outside
the peel is the outside, so the first and last letters of each word are taken
shredded vegetables are cut to bits, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: strip the outside of a chicken tikka and stir in grated carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peels from' takes the first and last letters of 'the' and of 'tikka', TE and TA; 'shredded' turns CARROT into RRACOT, which goes in between.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is the colour of unglazed fired clay, a brownish orange-red.

clue.text: Deficient Space Hopper

indicators.note: deficient means lacking, so the word is a letter short at the end

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A Space Hopper toy that is defective.
explanation.walkthrough: A Space Hopper is a bouncy rubber ball with handles, a children's toy; here the words split, and 'Hopper' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is short for kangaroo, an animal that moves by hopping.

clue.text: Dream crushed in work's dull routine

indicators.note: the scrambled dream goes inside the word for work

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

indicators.note: crushed means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dream crushed by the monotony of working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' turns DREAM into READM, which goes inside TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is figuratively any monotonous, wearying routine, after the old penal mill.

clue.text: Just like a man to fudge hard option

indicators.note: to fudge something is to fake or fiddle it, so these letters are juggled

explanation.surface: A dig at men: typical of one to dodge a difficult choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just like a man' reads as a sexist jibe but defines an adjective meaning resembling a human, as apes are said to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid means resembling a human being in form, used of the great apes.

clue.text: Powys town and its river are said to be disorganised

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.words: Powys town and its river are
parts.note: Hay-on-Wye is a book town in Powys, Wales, on the river Wye; then the word are

explanation.surface: A Welsh town and its river are in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY plus WYE plus ARE, said aloud, sound like the answer. Powys is a Welsh county.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to go out of control, so haywire means disorganised or chaotic.

clue.text: Gnaw on cold cut

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: Chewing over a slice of cold meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnaw on something is to bite at it repeatedly, a close synonym for working it with the teeth.

clue.text: Imperial rule overturned by knight, an unknown, in 1100

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the whole run is read from bottom to top
these pieces sit inside the Roman numerals for the date

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and C is 100
Sir is the title of a knight
an gives A, the indefinite article
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An empire overthrown by a knight and a mystery figure in medieval times.
explanation.definitionFit: Czarism is government by a czar, the autocratic imperial rule of the Russian emperors.

clue.text: Full of velocity, or rather fleet

indicators.note: one word is filled with another, the speed letter going inside

parts.note: nay is an old word used to correct oneself, meaning or rather
v is the symbol for velocity in physics

explanation.surface: Something packed with speed is quick, or rather swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like an adjective meaning swift, continuing the speed theme, but it is a noun: a body of warships.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a nation's fleet of warships, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Tree that quivers, quill-like?

parts.note: as means like
a quill was a pen made from a feather

explanation.surface: A tree with trembling leaves that look like feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar famous for leaves that tremble in the slightest breeze.

clue.text: For one who believes differently, skewed publicity!

definitions.text: For one who believes differently, skewed publicity!

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a pagan holds a faith other than the main world religions

indicators.note: skewed means twisted round, so the short word is turned back to front

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A slanted message in favour of a heathen is biased publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skewed' turns AD into DA. The whole clue is also the definition: biased publicity promoting one belief over another.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased or misleading publicity spread to promote a cause or point of view.

clue.text: Settled temperature in open

parts.note: over means finished, settled

explanation.surface: The weather settles to a mild temperature in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not concealed, the opposite of covert.

clue.text: Tons ceded in dispute, settling advantage

indicators.note: a dispute being settled is sorted out, so the remaining letters are rearranged
ceded means given up, so the tons letter leaves the dispute's letters

explanation.surface: A deal in a quarrel: giving up some tonnage to settle brings a gain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceded' removes T from DISPUTE, leaving DISPUE, and 'settling' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside of something is its benefit or good side, an advantage.

clue.text: Open vote with power in draw

indicators.note: the cross and power letters sit inside the word for draw

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out a response
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A public ballot with power to bring out a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective: stated plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated clearly and openly, with nothing hidden or implied.

clue.text: Competent person's advantage

definitions.meaning: a professional, someone skilled and capable at a job
a point in favour, as in the ... and cons of something

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: short for professional, and a point in favour of something.

clue.text: Neither remarkably absorbing nor primarily essential

indicators.note: one piece soaks up another, taking it inside
remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged
primarily takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something neither strikingly engrossing nor fundamentally important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges NEITHER (to INHERET) and that takes in N, the first letter of 'nor'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inherent quality is built in and intrinsic, part of the essential nature of a thing.

clue.text: Alloy preservative with uranium but not fluorine.

indicators.note: but not excludes something, so the fluorine letter is dropped

parts.note: formol is formalin, a preservative for specimens
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a preservative combined with uranium, but without any fluorine.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking F out of FORMOL plus U leaves the answer; all three elements keep the chemistry-lab surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is a gold-coloured alloy of copper and zinc used to decorate furniture.
